qa_pairs.question:
What do the sources say about periodic spending reports or summaries in personal finance apps — weekly, monthly or annual — including how they are delivered to the user (in-app, notification, email), which figures they contain, and whether users value or ignore them? Quote the relevant sentences with citations. If the sources do not cover this, say NOT IN SOURCES.

Separately: what do the sources say about "spending velocity heatmaps" as a feature of personal finance apps? Quote or say NOT IN SOURCES.
qa_pairs.answer:
### Periodic Spending Reports and Summaries in Personal Finance Apps

The sources discuss several aspects of periodic spending reports and summaries, including their delivery channels, frequencies, contents, and user reception.

#### 1. Delivery Methods and Frequency
Personal finance apps deliver spending summaries across daily, weekly, monthly, and annual intervals via emails, push notifications/alerts, and in-app dashboards:

* **Email Delivery**: Tiller sends a daily email digest: *"Daily Email Summary: Get a morning summary of your latest spending and balances"* [1].
* **Notifications & Alerts**: 
  * Rocket Money offers *"lots of notifications and reports to help you stay on top of your budget, including bill increase alerts and monthly spending reports."* [2]
  * PocketGuard provides periodic alerts: *"Notifications: Get weekly reports and alerts for fees, upcoming bills, and budget progress"* [3, 4].
  * Spendee uses push notifications: *"Alerts and reminders will notify you to pay the bill or not to exceed the budget."* [5].
* **In-App Dashboards & Recaps**:
  * Monarch Money provides *"weekly spending recaps"* [6] and allows users to compare spending across *"both monthly and annual time frames."* [7].
  * Copilot Money gives daily and monthly in-app overviews: *"Start your day with a quick look at your spending line, pending refunds, and upcoming bills."* [8] and *"Income up, expenses down. Track trends with monthly summaries."* [9].
  * PocketGuard offers a month-end review: *"Plan Tab Review: Access a month-end snapshot of your Plan to understand financial habits clearly"* [3, 10].
  * Wallet by BudgetBakers provides a *"clear overview of your cash flow for the month in an easy-to-navigate interface."* [11, 12].
  * Spendee delivers monthly financial tips: *"Get monthly money tips and stay on top of your finance"* [13].

---

#### 2. Figures and Details Contained
Periodic summaries and reports aggregate several key financial metrics:

* **Category and Retailer Breakdown**: PocketGuard's tool *"Breaks down your monthly spending into customizable categories, highlighting spending habits. It includes a 'merchants' section that adds up all the money spent at a given retailer each month."* [14]. It also tracks *"net income and transactions categorized by type, merchant, and more."* [15].
* **Cash Flow (Income vs. Expenses)**: Copilot Money tracks cash flow trends with *"Income up, expenses down"* [9], while Wallet by BudgetBakers *"shows expected net cash balances, making it easy for users to analyze their cash flow"* [12]. Actual Budget allows users to view custom weekly or monthly category breakdowns, such as *"how much was spent on food, by week, in both the Food and Restaurant categories over the last few months."* [16].
* **Account Balances, Debts, and Upcoming Bills**: Overviews consolidate broader balances; for instance, YNAB's dashboard lists *"account balances, loan debts and monthly bills."* [17], and Copilot Money includes pending items like *"spending line, pending refunds, and upcoming bills."* [8].

---

#### 3. Whether Users Value or Ignore Them
* **User Valuation**: The sources show that users value periodic reports, visual charts, and spending overviews for gaining financial awareness:
  * According to Forbes Consumer Sentiment data, *"Users appreciate the clear view of spending and monthly budgets with customizable categories and automations"* [18].
  * Wallet by BudgetBakers testing notes: *"The app is ideal for individuals who prefer data reports and easy-to-read graphics and charts to track their cash flow."* [19].
  * A user on Reddit noted: *"I like seeing where I spend my money, but I don't make real decisions on it. But it does show good insights."* [20].
  * A Copilot Money user shared: *"The graphs and analysis are beautiful. I'm able to see exactly where all my spend is going and plan for my future."* [21].
  * A PocketGuard user stated: *"PocketGuard has been a really helpful tool in understanding our family expenses... The extra functionality has been well worth it."* [22] and *"this is the first one that not only allowed me to understand my spending but also me to change my habits!!"* [23].
* **Ignoring Summaries**: **The sources do not mention whether users ignore periodic spending reports or summaries.**

---

### Spending Velocity Heatmaps

**NOT IN SOURCES.**

The sources do not mention or describe "spending velocity heatmaps" as a feature in personal finance apps. 

*(Note: The sources do mention PocketGuard's "Pace" feature, which *"alerts users if they're spending their budget too quickly based on how much money remains, and how many days are left in the month"* [24], but they do not mention heatmaps or the term "spending velocity heatmap".)*
